title: Lessons from Calloway; Dizzy, Joe Carroll and Moody
summary: He says Cab's band taught him booking and publicity, regrets losing Dizzy, and mentions Joe Carroll and James Moody.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Well, I'll tell you. I learned so much about the booking business and the personal management business just being with Calloway. By me being close to him, I saw all the things that Mills did, and the decisions that Cab made. And I learned that. Because I found out one thing about an artist. The one thing he's got to do is do something that appeals to the public. Because that's where you'll go, where you're going to be able to book them. They've got to be popular enough...
Because I did... Personally, I think I did a good job with Dizzy. I only had him for a year. I should have had him for a year with an option. But after I got him started,

I think that he and his wife thought that they didn't need me. Because I suggested to him to go to... I think I suggested to him to go to Willard Alexander... But no, he was already signed with Willard Alexander. I take that back. He was already signed with him. And then I didn't... I would have not agreed, if I had kept him, to let Joe Carroll go. Because Joe Carroll was an asset to him. But he still...
What about the other saxophone player that came around after, James Moody? Was he an asset to Dizzy?
Oh yeah. Moody was a great asset.
